title: Cross-Platform Operating-System Layer
objective: Make macOS, Linux, Windows native, and WSL2 first-class platform targets.

stories.title: Unix platform backend
stories.outcome: Implement macOS/Linux process, identity, allocated-size, notification, and filesystem semantics behind OS capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: macOS and Linux behavior uses explicit capability checks rather than cfg sprawl in domain code.
Unsupported filesystem features lower capability safely.
verification: macOS/Linux CI and filesystem integration suites.

stories.title: Windows native backend
stories.outcome: Implement Windows path, volume/file identity, reparse point, process, allocated-size, and atomic move semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Reparse points are never treated as Unix symlinks by assumption.
Drive/volume boundaries constrain quarantine and mutation.
verification: Windows CI with junction/symlink/reparse adversarial fixtures.

stories.title: WSL environment model
stories.outcome: Treat WSL as Windows host plus Linux guest/filesystem context rather than generic Linux.
acceptance_criteria: /mnt/* crossings are separately classified and performance/safety caveats surfaced.
verification: WSL integration smoke suite where available plus simulated path fixtures.

stories.title: Tiered platform support contract
stories.outcome: Publish Tier 1/Tier 2 platform capability matrix and support policy.
acceptance_criteria: No platform is called supported without required CI and destructive safety fixtures.
Unsupported OSes remain inspect-only or refused explicitly.
